name: load_after_copies
kind: redo of v2 with a lane-uniform stack chain: how non-bypass async copies displace stack lines from L1; no workload-based fitting
question: v2's chain indexed the stack array with a lane-dependent value, so every LDL was a 32-line gather - not the kernels' LDL [R1 + constant] (all lanes the same frame word, one line per warp). With a lane-uniform chain as in v1 (39 cycles per load at K = 0; +88 / +234 per load after 4 / 16 non-bypass copies): (1) how many of the chain's lines are lost per copy (K sweep); (2) does it need non-bypass copies and the same warp; (3) is the loss still there after the copies have returned; (4) does it depend on how many stack lines the chain cycles through and on the launch's shared-memory size?
probe: load_after_copies.cu, kernel k_lacl3<N, TW, FORM>: as k_lacl2 but the chain index is the same in every lane: per-thread volatile array of A words initialised loc[i] = (i + S) mod A with the same values in every thread, chain v = loc[v] started at a lane-independent word, so each LDL reads one frame word across the 32 lanes and the chain visits N distinct words. Axes: K in {0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32}; form ca / cg; issuer same_warp / other_warp; timing now / after_wait; chain length N in {2, 8}; array A in {64, 256} words (A = 64, N = 8 is the v1 cell); --smem extra dynamic shared memory in {0, 96 KiB, 200 KiB} (touched once; the 16-KiB copy ring stays). Cells: (a) K sweep x timing, ca, same_warp, N = 8, A = 64, smem 0; (b) cg and other_warp at K {0, 4, 16}; (c) N = 2 and A = 256 at K {0, 4, 16}; (d) smem {96 KiB, 200 KiB} at K {0, 4, 16}, now. 16 launches x 9 repetitions (first discarded), runs a and b; H100 and B300.

controls.sass: timed window: exactly N LDL, nothing else that touches memory, no barrier or wait.
controls.uniform: the host prints, for the first repetition, the word index every lane would read at each chain step (same formula as the kernel): all 32 equal.
controls.timing: A = 64, N = 8, now, ca, same_warp reproduces v1 (315 / 1015 / 2189 on h100 at K = 0 / 4 / 16) within 10 %; runs a and b within max(5 cycles, 5 %).

derivation: extra = C(K) - C(0); lost lines = extra / (L2 hit latency - L1 hit latency of the device) as an estimate; slope of lost lines over K.

predictions_before_data.displacement: extra grows with K until all N lines are lost (N x about 270 cycles), is the same now and after_wait and for other_warp, and is 0 for cg.
predictions_before_data.capacity: with larger shared memory (less L1) lines are lost at smaller K.

outcomes_before_data.rule: If the displacement predictions hold: rule = each line a non-bypass async copy brings through L1 evicts resident lines at a measured rate that applies to local-space lines (the engine's L1 gives stack lines no eviction pressure today); the form (per copied line, dependence on the carve-out) is stated in an addendum from cells (a) and (d) before the engine change.
outcomes_before_data.other: Otherwise report the table; addendum before any install.

prediction_check: H100 replay of A = 64, N = 8, now, ca, same_warp at K = 0, 4, 16 with the rule: C within max(30 cycles, 25 %) (main today: to be measured in the same replay); then the full-gpu 500 x 2 regression against main's baseline (fg-over20/full-gb).
not_allowed: No family / case / shape specific timing; no tuning to the full-gpu error; post-data changes of a criterion are labelled.

addenda.when: after h100-v3r1, b300-v3r1 and the H100 counter pass (data seen)
addenda.runs: $CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/microbench/load_after_copies/{h100-v3r1,b300-v3r1} (32 cells each, SASS gate and lane-uniformity check passed); counters $CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/fg-over20/lac-ncu (ncu, cache control none, 4 launches per cell); engine replay on main fg-over20/lac3-replay-table.txt
addenda.text: Control: the v1 cell is not reproduced within 10 % (259 / 764 / 1760 at K = 0 / 4 / 16 against v1's 315 / 1015 / 2189); v3 starts the chain at a different word every repetition where v1 started at a fixed one, so the two are different measurements; v3 is read on its own (stated after seeing the data). Chain of 8 uniform stack loads over a 64-word array, cycles (h100 / b300): K = 0 259 / 259 (32.4 per load); K = 1, 2 unchanged; K = 4 764 / 802; K = 8 1462 / 1387; K = 16 1760 / 1702; K = 32 2020 / 2147. The same after the copies have returned (after_wait) and when another warp issues them; bypass copies (cg) add nothing; 96 KiB or 200 KiB more dynamic shared memory change nothing. Chain of 2: +0 at K = 4, +246 / +273 at K = 16. 256-word array: 1731 / 1834 already at K = 0. Counters (h100, per launch = 72 stack loads): one stack load of 32 lanes is 4 sectors (288 sectors per launch) - local memory is interleaved by lane, a 4-byte frame word of a warp is one 128-byte line; with K = 0 every load sector is an L1 hit although the words were only stored before (a local store leaves its line in L1); non-bypass copies are 16 L1 sectors each, all lookup misses, and local-load sector misses per launch are 56-96 (K = 4), 212-228 (K = 16), 264-288 (K = 32), 0 for bypass copies; with the 256-word array (2048 local sectors stored at the start) 212-252 of 288 miss with no copies; the read sectors arriving from L2 equal copy sectors plus missed local sectors. Reading: outcome 'rule' in a more general form than declared - stack lines are ordinary residents of the SM's L1: stores and missed loads make them resident, everything that allocates in L1 (non-bypass copies, other stack lines, loads) pushes them out once the L1 is full, and a missed stack load is refilled from L2. The counts fit an L1 of about 640-760 sectors for this launch; the engine's carve-out model gives 640 (the carve-out is sized for the 13 CTAs of this shape that fit an SM, which is also why more shared memory changed nothing). The engine today keys a local access by the frame offset alone (one sector shared by all lanes and all warps of the SM), so the footprint is 32 x warps too small and stack lines are never pushed out (replay 420 at every K, and 52.5 per load where hardware has 32.4). Rule to install: (1) a local-memory access of width w at frame offset o by a warp covers the w sectors o .. o + w - 1 of that warp's own interleaved frame (each byte offset of 32 lanes is one sector); (2) a local store makes its sectors resident in L1; (3) a local load whose sectors are resident returns after the local hit latency (32.4 cycles on both devices, from K = 0), otherwise its sectors are fetched from L2 through the SM's L2 path at the L2 hit latency and become resident; (4) residency and eviction are those of the existing L1 model. Fields: l1 local_frame_interleaved (flag) and local_hit_latency_cycles, source load_after_copies v3 (h100 counters + timing; b300 timing, counters to follow), experimental until the replay passes. Replay criterion (medians over repetitions 1-8 of the traced launch, the probe's statistic): K = 0, 4, 8, 16, 32 within max(60 cycles, 25 %) of the hardware medians. The replay starts with an empty L1 and one launch, so the criterion at K = 4 is recorded but not binding (hardware's L1 is pre-filled by the warm-up kernel).
